illustration.alt: Max Abelson speaks into a Bloomberg podcast microphone beside an AMC-versus-Robinhood placard, a blockchain stock ledger, and bearer certificates slipping from a heist bag.

elementaryChecklist.financialMechanism: A stock ledger records who owns shares and may be maintained on a blockchain; bearer securities give important rights to the person physically holding the documents, so stealing them can enable a thief to claim or transfer value.
elementaryChecklist.centralJoke: The podcast crams an absurdly broad procession of topics—from Kawhi Leonard and bearer-security heists to finance aesthetics, geniality rankings, and choosing contextually appropriate “oohs”—into one episode.

preschool.title: Max and the Very Crowded Microphone
preschool.lesson: Stock ledgers record share ownership and can be kept on a blockchain, while bearer securities depend on physical possession—making the documents tempting targets for theft.
paragraphs:
At Bloomberg, Max Abelson took the guest chair,
A senior reporter with questions to spare.
Money Stuff started with money and power,
Then talked Kawhi Leonard within the same hour.

Independent investigations joined the cascade,
Along with the curious DAT trade.
“Why does anyone talk to us?” floated nearby,
Then finance’s beauty drew an aesthetic eye.

Robinhood faced AMC in the chatter,
While meme-stock bazaars made everything madder.
Cede & Co. came up; stock ledgers came next—
Could blockchain record who owns shares in its text?

Grayson Moorhead Securities joined the array,
Then bearer-security heists stole the day.
Those papers reward whoever holds them just right,
So thieves might steal ownership clear out of sight.

The Apollo premium earned a review,
Then geniality league tables lined up in a queue.
After that whirlwind, one puzzle remained:
Which “ooh” fits the context when finance is explained?

The episode’s out on Spotify and Apple,
With enough odd ideas for a week’s worth of babble.
Money, basketball, markets, and crooks—
All squeezed in together, with finance judged on its looks.

What happened? Bloomberg released a Money Stuff podcast episode guest-hosted by senior reporter Max Abelson. Its topics included blockchain stock ledgers, which record share ownership, and bearer securities, whose reliance on physical possession makes theft especially consequential.
